subject: Request: PraxisAI POC concession — one-time tier reshuffle (VP/CFO sign-off needed)
messages:
From: Lena Ortega <lena@praxisai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PraxisAI POC — ask for concession and tier tweak

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — team was impressed with the latency and batching guidance you gave. We're ready to kick off a 3-month POC but have a hard constraint on upfront spend from procurement. The ask from our CFO is a one-time concession in the first 90 days combined with a temporary tier reshuffle so we can burst for a launch pilot.

Requested items:
- One-time credit of $30k to offset initial evaluation usage.
- Temporarily move PraxisAI from Starter -> Tier 2 (up to 200k tokens/month) for the first 90 days to avoid throttles during the pilot, then revert.
- 60-day invoice terms (we know it's outside standard).

I attached our projected MAU/usage (.xlsx) and a short note on procurement constraints (concession_request.pdf). Can we get an indication on whether Redwood can accommodate? This is a strategic POC — likely to expand with a commercial contract if successful.

Appreciate any flexibility — happy to hop on a quick call.

— Lena

Attachments: praxisai_mau_forecast.xlsx, concession_request.pdf

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: PraxisAI POC — ask for concession and tier tweak

Team — forwarding PraxisAI's ask. Quick summary: external asks for $30k one-off credit, temporary tier bump for 90 days, and 60-day terms. They position this as a strategic POC with high expansion potential.

My read: high upside but material near-term revenue giveback. Marcus, can you run a 12-month NPV/recoup model if we grant a partial concession? Marissa, what's the precedent for temporary tier reshuffles and 60-day terms for POCs? Karthik, any procurement/legal flags on the term-length/contract amendment side?

Goal: decide whether to approve an exception and draft an exec memo for VP/CFO sign-off. If we escalate, I suggest we propose a compromise (see below) before sending to execs.

Suggested compromise (my draft):
- Offer $18k one-time credit (60% of ask) tied to a signed LOA within 5 business days.
- Approve temporary tier bump to Tier 2 for 60 days (not 90), with automatic reversion unless usage exceeds the threshold for three consecutive weeks.
- Standard 30-day terms for first invoice; finance to consider 60-day for subsequent based on credit checks.

If you agree, I'll prepare the escalation memo. Please reply with any hard no/yes by EOD so we can respond to PraxisAI.

Thanks,
Mina
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: PraxisAI POC — ask for concession and tier tweak

Mina — thanks for the note and good summary. A few points: 

1) Precedent: We have granted one-off credits for POCs in the 10–25k range, but $30k is above typical. Temporary tier bumps are unusual but have been allowed when engineering confirms low operational risk. 60-day net is uncommon without finance approval.

2) Risks: If we allow a 90-day bump we need an explicit reversion and an engineer/ops contact to monitor KV cache behavior — avoid overprovisioning. Also need to lock the credit so it's not applied if they churn within 30 days.

3) Approval path: This requires VP/CFO sign-off due to the size and terms. I'm fine escalating with the compromise you suggested but would tighten it: $15k credit, 45-day tier bump, 45-day payment terms for first invoice. We can tie additional credits to milestone-based consumption.

I've attached a short concession memo skeleton for exec review (concession_exec_memo.docx). If you want me to lead the ask to VP/CFO, I will.

— Marissa
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: concession_exec_memo.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: PraxisAI POC — ask for concession and tier tweak

Quick legal/procurement flags: 
- 60-day terms will require procurement to sign off and likely an updated SOW or LOA. We should avoid amending the master services agreement for a short POC; instead use an LOA (Letter of Authorization) that references the standard T&Cs and lists the temporary tier and credit.
- Ensure the credit language includes clawback for churn within 30 days and a clear definition of "pilot success" tied to conversion milestones.
- I can draft the LOA template once the concession amount and term are finalized.

No major redlines otherwise.

— Karthik
Senior Counsel, Commercial

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: PraxisAI POC — ask for concession and tier tweak

Ran the numbers on the attached financial_impact_model.xlsx. Short summary:
- At $30k credit + 90-day tier bump we see an immediate ARR dilution effect ~ $72k over 12 months (assuming conservative 35% conversion).
- If we offer a $15k credit + 45-day bump and structure the remainder as milestone-based credits (payable upon a conversion milestone), the 12-month dilution drops to ~$28k and we retain upside capture.
- Cashflow impact: extending net terms to 60 days increases working capital pressure; finance would prefer 30 days for first invoice with an option to move to 45 days after credit review.

Recommendation (finance): Approve a controlled concession: $15k one-time credit, 45-day tier bump, credit clawback if customer doesn't convert in 120 days, and 30-day initial payment term. If Marissa/Minas want to preserve deal momentum, tie additional credits to concrete milestones.

I can sign off operationally if the concession is capped at these terms — otherwise this needs VP/CFO explicit approval.

— Marcus
Director, Revenue Finance
Attachment: financial_impact_model.xlsx

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortega <lena@praxisai.com>, Tom Sweeney <tom.sweeney@praxisai.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Final: PraxisAI concession proposal for VP/CFO decision — please review

Thanks all for fast turnaround — below is the memo I'll escalate to VP/CFO (Marissa, feel free to edit). I copied PraxisAI so they're aware this is awaiting exec review.

Executive memo (for VP/CFO):

Subject: Exception request — PraxisAI POC concession (one-time credit + temporary tier bump)

Background: PraxisAI requests a one-time $30k credit and a 90-day bump to Tier 2 for a three-month POC. They are a mid-market AI startup with a product-led sales motion; the POC is intended to validate a production launch with an expected commercial expansion. Procurement requires extended terms, and they provided a usage forecast attached.

Proposal (recommended):
- One-time credit: $15,000 applied to first invoice; an additional $10,000 available as milestone-based credits upon agreed conversion milestones (total potential concession $25,000).
- Temporary Tier: Approve Tier 2 for 45 days (automatic reversion unless extended by mutual written agreement).
- Payment terms: Standard 30-day terms for first invoice; finance to review eligibility for 45-day terms after first payment clears.
- Contracting: Use an LOA referencing the existing MSA. Include clawback clause: credit forfeited if customer does not convert within 120 days.

Commercial impact: Finance estimates ~ $28k ARR dilution in the first 12 months under the recommended terms with upside if conversion occurs.

Decision requested: VP/CFO approval to grant the above exception. If approved, legal to draft LOA and sales to execute within 5 business days.

Attachments: praxisai_mau_forecast.xlsx, concession_request.pdf, financial_impact_model.xlsx

Next steps: If approved, Marissa will prepare the official exec memo and add sign-off block for VP and CFO. If not approved, sales will present the counteroffer ($5k credit + 30-day bump) to PraxisAI.

Mina
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

---
On behalf of PraxisAI: Lena/Tom — we should hear back within 24 hours of exec sign-off. If you can push procurement to accept a 30-day initial invoice, that would help move this quickly.

Attachments: praxisai_mau_forecast.xlsx, concession_request.pdf, financial_impact_model.xlsx
